sourceReview.SIAndPhysicalSign: History remains SI: duration_s is seconds, energy is Wh, SoC differences are percentage points. Qualified drive drop must be positive and at most 50 points, duration positive and at most 24h; completed charging gain must be positive. Negative/nonfinite energy is excluded from energy totals, missing energy stays null, measured zero Wh remains a valid observed value. No battery diagnosis, total-energy inference from SoC, capacity estimate, AC/DC substitution, electricity-rate advice or command mutation is introduced.
sourceReview.measuredVersusModeled: Current/endpoint SoC and completed charging Wh are source observations. Scenario means/percentiles, support score, reserve crossing and guidance are modeled descriptive results; wording explicitly states omitted inputs and no promised outcome. P75 presentation and provenance/readiness issues remain findings.
sourceReview.denominators: Burn distribution counts active qualified local days; weekday profiles use every calendar occurrence in the configured window; energy totals disclose energyRows; row categories assign each returned row once. Direct final source confirms mark() increments includedRows at line 500, separately from inWindowRows at lines 639/725; no double-count finding is asserted.
sourceReview.readiness: Model requires 28 observed-span days, 8 active local days and 4 active weeks for actionable guidance, with charging-state precedence and unavailable/stale current-state rejection. It does not gate on full history coverage, history cap, query retention or replay mode.
sourceReview.preferences: useUnits energy formatter consumes raw Wh and existing locale/precision; useNumberFormatting subscribes to preference changes; useTimezone('vehicle') uses existing vehicle/user/browser resolution. Reserve floor 10/20/30 is a page-local business scenario control, not a duplicate workspace selector. Calendar IDs/technical identifiers are not automatically translated. Timing and accessible numeric-table formatting remain findings.
sourceReview.loading: History sources have independent availability/loading flags. Live-source provenance and independent drive-only/charging-only sections can survive a neighbor loading. Both-dependent content and KPI aggregate loading remain bounded issues; no runtime render was performed.
sourceReview.fatal: Only useDataState fatalError produces the initial QueryError surface; successful independent sources are not globally discarded. The one retry callback refetches errored history sources. Both-source section content loss is recorded below.
sourceReview.retained: Cached history arrays remain in the model on refresh failure; one KPI warning/retry is shown and OperationalBrief marks retained source evidence. Paused source warnings are present at page lines 164-177 with source-specific refresh, not an offline/server-failure invention. Local sections still receive simplified trust state and no last-success age.
sourceReview.emptyAndMalformed: No vehicle keeps 13 source shell declarations with select-vehicle messages. Missing SoC statistics remain em dashes in most displays; scenario/trend empty states are explanatory. The model rejects invalid/future/incomplete rows into accounting categories, normalizes invalid options/timezones and avoids mutating inputs. No bad response was created or injected. History shape loss and zero-filled weekdays remain findings.
sourceReview.recovery: History retry invokes only errored queries; paused warnings use their own DataState retry. Live recovery re-reads the canonical live query on a proven reconnect and handles visibility/cooldown; Pub/Sub is not represented as durable replay. Reconnect/out-of-order behavior was not executed.
sourceReview.actions: Actual page actions are local reserve selection, read retries, OperationalBrief details and shared chart controls/export. No apply-charge-limit, charging schedule, Fleet API command, vehicle/config write, notification or advice mutation call occurs in page source. As-of write authorization is therefore not claimed broken; the finding concerns unguarded current recommendation evidence.

findings.mechanism: meanPath stores p75EndSocPct from meanSoc. The real p75Soc is written only to p75Path. Both the chart and directory consume meanPath for the displayed p75 end SoC, so the labeled p75 path/end values duplicate the mean even when p75 burn differs. Guidance and reserve sensitivity use p75Path, allowing visible paths to disagree with their crossing results.
findings.existingEvidence: The existing model fixture at chargeAdvisor.test.ts:258-286 explicitly has a weekday mean greater than zero and calendar p75 zero, and another with mean 5/p75 10. No response or execution was manufactured.
findings.followUp: Make each displayed ScenarioDay carry the actual paired mean/p75 end values, or have the two display consumers join the actual paths. Preserve raw values, dates, series/export/table fields and verify differing paths and crossing agreement through an assigned owner.
findings.runtimeProof: Still required; this report does not claim a captured production misrender.

findings.mechanism: Page uses aggregate signalCount > 0 as proof that batteryLevel, isCharging and chargeLimitSoc were observed. The live hook initializes those independent fields to 0/false/0 and signalCount counts all received keys, not those fields. Thus unrelated signal presence promotes absent battery/charging/limit values to measured facts; validSoc accepts zero, defeating unknown-vs-zero and potentially selecting a fictitious 0% live candidate over a valid historical endpoint.
findings.followUp: Have the existing live owner expose field-specific presence/validity for BatteryLevel, charging-state evidence and ChargeLimitSoc. The page must pass null for unobserved fields without treating a genuine observed 0% as missing. Parent assigns the shared owner; no competing page-side live store.
findings.runtimeProof: Requires a real permitted missing-field/partial-signal observation later; none was injected here.

findings.mechanism: Actual live wire includes per-field ts/timestamp/source/age_ms. Hook flattening retains only value and stamps browser receipt time as lastUpdated; any partial SSE update also restamps the merged retained battery. Page labels that receipt 'live' and model uses the same two-day fallback threshold for live validity. Backend classifies live values stale after two minutes and legacy zero timestamps as unknown-freshness L2, but that evidence cannot reach this page. Retained/stale/unknown-freshness values can therefore appear fresh and support current guidance.
findings.followUp: Preserve source timestamps/age/classification per relevant field through the existing live boundary. Separate the two-minute live freshness contract from the explicitly disclosed historical endpoint fallback policy; do not refresh a field's observed time on an unrelated message.
findings.runtimeProof: Real wire, reconnect and delayed/out-of-order source-time proof remains pending.

findings.mechanism: A both-dependent section replaces all children when either history source is missing and replaces them with loading content while either initially loads. Accounting loses the successful source's counts/categories; static methodology disappears; a valid drive_end fallback requires unrelated charging availability and vice versa. All shells survive, but independent evidence and the definitions needed to interpret remaining guidance do not. KPI loading is similarly whole-brief rather than per independent metric.
findings.followUp: Render accounting sources independently, leave static methodology available, select current-state dependency from its actual source and preserve independent KPI values. Keep missing-source explanations and individual recovery without a page-wide gate.

findings.mechanism: Actual dated history page is absent from RANGE_ENABLED_PATHS and never consumes useRangeState. Its queries send only vehicle_id and limit, and the model uses its own fixed 180-day clock/window. Consequently shared from/to URL/preferences cannot scope these history results or aggregates, contrary to the current workspace date-bound contract. No duplicate local date/vehicle selector is present.
minimalFollowUpScope: existing bounded history hooks and directly matching tests
findings.followUp: Parent resolves/assigns date ownership and wires both header-owned instants through typed, isolated keys and complete server-bound history. Preserve explicitly approved independent tomorrow-first planning semantics; do not add a second date picker or silently replace the accepted model.
findings.runtimeProof: Rolling/custom/DST bounds and complete server result proof remain required; no endpoint request was made.

findings.mechanism: Every calendar date absent from qualified returned drives becomes zero burn, including before the earliest returned observation and dates with only excluded/unqualified rows. Weekday metrics therefore become numeric zero even with no qualified evidence, while active-day distribution correctly remains null. The 1000-row cap is only disclosed; it is not part of the readiness gate. A span/active-day gate can pass without proving that the entire 180-day denominator was observed, diluting means/percentiles and supporting 'No immediate need' from unproven no-use dates.
findings.existingEvidence: Existing page fixture supplies eight May 2026 drive dates while the model default calendar spans 180 days. Existing model fixture intentionally distinguishes zero calendar p75 from positive active-day use; no invented bad response is needed to establish the source assumption.
minimalFollowUpScope: parent-assigned history coverage owner if a complete observation window is required
findings.followUp: Keep intended calendar-day versus active-day definitions explicit, but distinguish observed no-driving dates from unknown/excluded/capped coverage. Withhold recommendation readiness or label the assumption when coverage is not established; do not present absent qualified evidence as measured 0% use.
findings.runtimeProof: Actual history coverage/recording completeness and bounded pagination require future permitted source/wire evidence.

findings.mechanism: Page does not consume as_of/operational mode. History/live keys and reads remain present-time, analysis clock starts at Date.now, realtime subscription is enabled, and readiness can yield current charge guidance even on an as_of URL. The existing request operational guard is mutation-only and cannot guard these read/model outputs. There is no page mutation, so this is not a claimed unsafe queued write.
findings.followUp: Use the existing operational-mode owner to disclose and block live recommendation readiness in replay/cached contexts, or consume an explicitly supported historical snapshot contract. Do not invent historical advice capability or a new replay engine.
findings.runtimeProof: Mounted as-of/live/cached transitions and shell mode interaction require future proof.

findings.mechanism: Both selected history hooks use safeArray, which warns and replaces a non-array result with []. The page regards resolved data/isSuccess as available and the pure model further normalizes non-arrays to []. An unexpected shape therefore cannot remain distinguishable from an authoritatively successful empty history; fatal/error recovery is not activated and the original shape is unavailable to accounting.
findings.followUp: An assigned hook owner should validate analytical-history shape and retain prior valid data on shape failure, rather than changing safeArray globally. Preserve the legitimate backend [] empty contract and row-level category accounting.
findings.runtimeProof: No malformed response was manufactured, fetched or injected; this is the observable source branch, not a reported production incident.

findings.mechanism: Charging start hours are assembled as fixed ASCII HH:00, bypassing existing locale/time display formatting. Both chart callers provide numeric accessible columns without kind or format; the actual fallback Table then uses String(raw), bypassing the subscribed numeric precision/locale that the cards use. Technical IDs/date keys need not be translated, and raw numeric exports must remain numeric.
findings.followUp: Use the existing time-display boundary for already-local hour buckets and the existing chart column numeric rendering contract. Preserve source-local bucket meaning, raw export values, stable identities and all table columns; no shared formatter/catalog rewrite.
findings.runtimeProof: Actual locale/precision/time-preference and screen-reader presentation remains NOTRUN.

findings.mechanism: Scoped case-sensitive source scan finds 12 hardcoded text-size class overrides on Text rather than the existing typography/metric roles. Repeated informational values also receive fixed cyan emphasis. Shared UI usage alone does not establish saved font-scale, neutral hierarchy or theme-safe contrast compliance.
findings.followUp: Use existing MetricValue/Caption/Text roles and semantic foreground tokens while retaining every value, caption, denominator and null state. Do not invent another BatteryMetricCard or change shared typography/theme owners.
findings.runtimeProof: No measured contrast, clipping or visual failure is claimed; composed theme/font/matrix proof is still required.
